children: San Juan Basin reported that it will not declare a monthly cash distribution for September 2026 due to cumulative excess production costs of approximately $12,553,466 gross ($9,415,100 net to the Trust) and continued low natural gas prices. Hilcorp reported July 2026 revenue from the subject interests of $4,293,096 and production costs (excluding excess cost balance) of $5,415,731 for the month. The trust drew $44,606 from its line of credit to cover administrative expenses and will not distribute funds until excess costs, a $2,000,000 reserve, and line-of-credit principal and interest are repaid.
Total reported revenue from the subject interests for July 2026: $4,293,096 (gas $4,116,328; oil $176,768).
Production costs for July 2026 (excluding excess production cost balance): $5,415,731 (lease operating expenses $2,918,257; severance taxes $385,466; capital costs $2,112,008).
Cumulative excess production costs balance: approximately $12,553,466 gross ($9,415,100 net to the Trust), an increase of $1,122,634 gross ($841,976 net) from prior month.

Trust administrative expenses for the month: $44,628; interest income $23 and a $44,606 draw from the line of credit used to pay these expenses, bringing the outstanding line-of-credit principal to $1,075,400.
Cash reserves maintained by the Trust: $3,891 (unchanged from prior month).
Trust will not receive royalty income while Hilcorp continues to apply all net proceeds to the balance of excess production costs resulting from drilling two new horizontal wells in 2024.

No cash distributions will be made until future net proceeds are sufficient to (a) repay the excess production costs balance, (b) replenish a $2,000,000 reserve, and (c) repay principal and interest on the Trust’s line of credit.

Gas volumes for July 2026 totaled 2,046,556 Mcf (2,273,951 MMBtu), up from 1,950,221 Mcf (2,166,912 MMBtu) in June 2026; average gas price for July 2026 was $2.01 per Mcf ($1.81 per MMBtu), up $0.55 per Mcf versus June.

Production continues to be gathered, processed and sold under market-sensitive customary agreements; Trustee and third-party auditors are conducting ongoing audits of Hilcorp’s accounting, pricing, and payments to the Trust.
